title: Denver Downtown 16th Street Food Tour
includes: Flaky French Quiche Made with Green Chiles
Argentinian Empanadas from a Local Shop
Colorado Bison Chili with Black Beans and White Cheddar
Handmade Pork Dumplings from a Family-Owned Restaurant
requirements: Infants and small children can ride in a pram or stroller
All areas and surfaces are wheelchair accessible
Suitable for all physical fitness levels
Not recommended for travelers with dietary restrictions (dairy-free, vegan, gluten free)
cancellation: For a full refund, cancel at least 24 hours before the scheduled departure time.
blurb: What makes this tour unique is the way it combines Denver’s evolving downtown story with flavors from the local businesses shaping it today. Guests begin at the historic Brown Palace, then explore the newly redesigned 16th Street while seeing landmarks such as the Colorado State Capitol, Denver Pavilions, Paramount Theatre, Skyline Park, and the Daniels & Fisher Clock Tower. Along the way, the tour stops at four locally owned restaurants for a diverse lineup of tastings, including bison chili, empanadas, handmade pork potstickers, and green chile quiche. Rather than focusing on just one cuisine, the experience shows how immigrant-owned businesses, Colorado ingredients, and international food traditions all come together in downtown Denver. It is part walking tour, part history lesson, and part progressive meal, giving guests a deeper sense of the city through both its architecture and its food.
